question: How far apart are the robot's final and initial positions?
Measure the direct distance in the horizontal XY plane and ignore obstacles.
For how much of the recording was the robot stationary?
Stationary means moving slower than 0.08 m/s.
Treat brief movement lasting at most 1 second as part of the same stop.
Ignore stops shorter than 2 seconds.
When did the robot walk backward relative to the direction its body was facing?
The robot must be moving faster than 0.10 m/s while its forward speed is below -0.08 m/s.
Join backward periods separated by gaps of at most 0.5 seconds.
Only report intervals lasting at least 1 second.
How many times did the robot's simplified path cross itself?
Simplify the path with a 0.10 m Ramer-Douglas-Peucker tolerance.
Only count proper crossings between nonadjacent path segments at least 5 seconds apart.
Merge nearby crossings into one event when they occur within 2 seconds and 0.30 m.
Report the average later-crossing time for each merged event.
How much can the robot's XY path be simplified into straight segments?
Use Ramer-Douglas-Peucker with a 0.20 m tolerance and ignore collisions.
Compare the original and simplified lengths and count turns of at least 20 degrees.
A segment is backward when its median cosine alignment with body yaw is negative.
For stationary rotations, use speed below 0.08 m/s, bridge movement gaps of at most 1 second,
ignore stops shorter than 2 seconds, and require at least 30 degrees of net unwrapped rotation.
Where did the robot later travel back along a path it had previously followed?
Compare 2-second movement windows that are at least 10 seconds apart.
Their midpoint locations must be within 0.30 m and directions at least 150 degrees apart.
Join matching periods across gaps of at most 0.5 seconds.
Report the longest match lasting at least 1 second and its most recent earlier path.
Which location did the robot leave and return to after the longest time?
The two positions must be within 0.30 m and at least 10 seconds apart.
Between them, the robot must have traveled at least 1 m away from the earlier position.
Report the midpoint of the matching positions and the elapsed time.
When was the robot facing most directly away from its direction of travel?
Compare body direction with movement over each centered 2-second window.
Only consider windows where movement speed is at least 0.10 m/s.
Report the window with the largest angle between body direction and travel direction.
